correctness.rationale: For complete multipartite G=K_(n1,…,nr), r≥2, inclusion-maximal matchings have an independent unmatched-vertex set, necessarily empty or contained in exactly one part. The empty case contributes the perfect-matching count for even N. For a nonempty unmatched set choose its unique part and u vertices; the residual graph must admit a perfect matching, giving the stated binomial-weighted polynomial without overcount. The perfect-matching sum follows by cross-part edge multiplicities; residual perfect matching exists iff its largest part has ≤ half the even residual order. This proves the exact size-spectrum condition and first-moment mean, including complete graphs, odd N, and unbalanced part profiles. Independent brute-force edge-disjoint matching enumeration matched every polynomial coefficient for 58 nondecreasing multipartite profiles on 2–8 vertices (2,448 maximal matchings); the all-orders assertion follows from the matching-to-residual bijection, not enumerated data.
residual_risks: Finite independent enumerations are corroboration only; the all-parameter conclusion rests on the reconstructed symbolic proof.
